I recently added a lightweight literate programming system to Verso. Because this didn't exist when this project was started, @Pim Otte wrote custom code based on Verso to generate a site from the Lean development. Now, I don't think this custom code is necessary anymore. Thank you for developing the stopgap, @Pim Otte!

Here's a pull request.

Here's a summary of the differences:

  • The site looks a bit different, but the basic visual and logical structure is the same. It now has light and dark modes. Code is rendered with the same Verso library, so it still works the same way. Here's a screenshot:

  • Verso's integrated search feature is used. It allows searching the both the names of definitions and the text itself, with full-text search using a standard heuristic word stemming system so e.g. searching for "preference" also yields results for "prefers".

  • The build process is greatly simplified. Instead of having two internal projects on different Lean versions and a build system that orchestrates them, there is a single project that merely has an extra Verso dependency, with a TOML file to configure things like custom chapter titles. Building the HTML is one command: lake build :literateHtml.

  • The whole site builds much more quickly.

  • Docstrings are all written in Verso. Verso is mostly like Markdown, but it allows you to annotate code snippets that explain whether they're a tactic name, a Lean term, etc. This means you get red squigglies in your IDE for typos, instead of having view the rendered result to find out. It also means that everything is accurately highlighted, so the tactic intro is kept separate from the constructor True.intro.

One thing that this literate programming system does not yet do is integrate with doc-gen4's output. The code that this site is replacing had this integration. As I understand it, this integration was mainly to enable search, so I think the built-in Verso search makes that unnecessary. If there are further use cases that I'm not aware of, please let me know and I'll see what I can do.

Search was part of it, another reason doc-gen4 is included is to help newcomers get used to what they'd find if they moved on to doing something with mathlib. That function does not rely on the integration, just on it existing. If the lean action still builds the doc-gen, everything I can think of is covered:)

I took that out to speed up the build, but I'll put it back in.

In the current site, the doc-gen output has its own navbar entry. The literate programming feature in Verso doesn't have a simple way to add external links to the navigation bar.

I think that a thing that isn't linked to might as well not exist. Do you think it is sufficient to put a link to it on the landing page?

Personally, I think that would be sufficient but I want to defer to @Terence Tao, since this was his explicit requirement. Things also might have shifted over time on this front.

I deployed this to my repo so it's reviewable by clicking through: https://pimotte.github.io/analysis-ci

Looks very nice!

Does the new Verso format support links? For instance, if in the docstring for Proposition X I want to make a reference to Lemma Y with a clickable link to that lemma, could that be done through suitable tagging similar to HTML?

The answer is "Yes" with a bit of a caveat: it only works for backwards references so far. We're working on lifting this limitation.

The way Verso works is that while Lean is checking the file, it also checks the contents of the docstring. An annotation like {name} indicates that some code is a name, for example. While the file is being checked, if the name isn't found then it's an error; Lean also provides the usual interactive features like hovers and go-to-definition:

In the rendered output, the name becomes a link and gets a hover automatically. Because you're telling it the right name while writing the document, there's no heuristic step that might link to the wrong Sum. Whichever is in scope in the original file is the one that's used:

Ah, okay. I imagine that the doc-gen files will look slightly uglier due to the added tags? I suppose if we intend the Verso to be a complete replacement for the doc-gen then this is not really an issue.

Lean internally converts the Verso format to Markdown for clients that don't know how to interpret Verso, so this particular comment looks like this:

This conversion process loses some information, but it's no worse than having written plain Markdown to start with. Soon, doc-gen will have native support for Verso along with Markdown, so the lossy step won't be needed.

The plan is more a convergence of Verso and doc-gen, with the former used for technical writing (user manuals, blueprints, textbooks, lecture notes, in-file documentation) and the latter being a great way to find out what is available with my current set of dependencies.
I see you merged it! Please don't hesitate to get in touch if anything needs updating or modification, or if you need any other support with it.

It seems like merging a previously outstanding PR has somehow broken the build in a way that even reverting that PR does not fix, see https://github.com/teorth/analysis/pull/476 . The error message is

Run lake build
error: /home/runner/work/analysis/analysis/.lake/packages/mathlib: could not resolve 'HEAD' to a commit; the repository may be corrupt, so you may need to remove it and try again
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

Not sure how to repair this, any suggestions?

I'm far from a computer until Tuesday, but there may be something wrong with the cache. Perhaps try deleting the caches from the last few days and see if it improves? Here's some instructions: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manage-caches#deleting-cache-entries
Reverting + clearing the cache seems to work (at least for the initial CI), hopefully the previous PR can be resubmitted and it will work this time.
Would you like me to generate a PR that reverts the revert?
When going to do it, it seems that the simplified theorems are no longer present, having been superseded by Mathlib theorems, so I don't think that reversion of the reversion is needed :)
